clue.text: Monsieur's not out of sorts — just out of place!

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, and the 's stands for 'is', giving M plus IS
someone not out of sorts is well, in good health, so fit

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who is not grumpy but simply feels he does not belong.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Monsieur's has to be read as 'is', so it supplies letters too.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is a person who does not suit their surroundings, someone who simply does not belong.

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to contend is to compete, to vie, so contended is vied

explanation.surface: The wine god wearing a crown, and one rival who competed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacchus, the Roman god of wine, was pictured wreathed in ivy leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus wears a wreath of ivy, so he is covered or crowned with ivy.

indicators.note: for a change makes the gathered letters swap into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, the second Gospel writer's name, which also means target

explanation.surface: Someone saying 'skeleton' is what we score for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 across answer joins WE and FOR, and 'a change' rearranges the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework is the supporting structure of something, its skeleton.

definitions.meaning: one who counts, such as a bank clerk at a counter or a vote counter
one who tells, relates or reports

explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier or vote counter is so called, and so is someone who tells, a narrator or informant.

parts.note: the question seems to be about a historian, but the second word turns it into natural history, the study of plants among other living things

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether some scholar studies history, answered 'naturally'.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'history? Naturally' together as natural history, of which the study of plant life is a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist of plant life works in one branch of natural history.

clue.text: Old policeman confounded Turner? No, Webster

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A quiz answer: a painter? No, the dictionary-maker, says a puzzled contestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confounded' rearranges TURNER NO WEBSTER, all fifteen letters. Bow Street Runners were London's early police force, set up in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional constables, based at the Bow Street magistrates' court.

clue.text: Instead perhaps cut up those becoming jumpers

annotationWithheld.why: Instead perhaps cut up those becoming jumpers (8) for TADPOLES: the scan confirms the text, but no reading of 'Instead perhaps cut up' builds TADPOLES (INSTEAD's letters do not fit)
annotationWithheld.clue: Instead perhaps cut up those becoming jumpers

indicators.note: back says the word for half is read in reverse

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Name a half-back to play for a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-back' looks like the football position, but it is two parts: half (SEMI) and back, which reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, famous for its Roman arena.

parts.note: sur is the French word for on
to render a wall is to coat it with plaster

explanation.surface: Giving way on a French kind of plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to surrender is to give up or hand over, as an army gives way to an enemy.

clue.text: Terribly slow lead I'd not permitted

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a leader was dreadfully sluggish and they were refused permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges SLOW LEAD I'D, ten letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disallowed has been refused or forbidden, so it is not allowed.

parts.note: something for me is mine, my own
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone declaring a particular woman painter is their favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: the answer is a woman's name. RA comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it can stand for any female person referred to as she.

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
upsets means the poet's name is knocked over and its letters disordered

parts.note: Beatrice is an example of a woman, referred to as her

explanation.surface: A follower is annoyed that Dante wrote about his muse Beatrice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsets' rearranges DANTE into ADENT, and 'about' wraps that round HER, with Beatrice standing for any woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or leader, as a disciple is.

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something partly wrecks a borer shell or a bivalve mollusc.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'or lamellibranch' as the definition, but 'or' is only a link word; the definition is 'lamellibranch'. The answer runs across 'destroys terebra'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamellibranch is a bivalve mollusc with plate-like gills, such as a mussel, clam or this shellfish.

parts.note: two's company, three's a crowd: a group of three is no company, and a group of three musicians plays together

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a band are poor company.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes a group of three 'no company'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three players or singers performing together.

clue.text: Boisterous' actors are going to the wall

parts.note: rough can mean boisterous, unruly
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Rowdy actors are being ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to the wall' looks like failing; read literally it is plaster applied to walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a coarse plaster of lime and gravel spread on outside walls.

clue.text: Happening to die perhaps late in the day

parts.note: a happening is an event, something that occurs

indicators.note: perhaps says the short word that follows may be read in some other order

explanation.surface: An event leading someone to die, possibly late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges DIE into IDE, which follows EVENT; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Patterns the Army turns into places of worship

indicators.note: into says that piece goes inside the next

parts.note: temples are buildings for religious worship

indicators.note: turns says the abbreviation for the army is reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve army

explanation.surface: Soldiers transform church buildings according to designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' reverses TA (Territorial Army, the British army reserve) to AT, which goes 'into' TEMPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Templates are shaped guides used to reproduce a design, so they are patterns.

definitions.meaning: Harry ... was a popular English music-hall singer, of 'Any Old Iron' fame
excellent, the best, in an old colloquial use

explanation.definitionFit: Music-hall star Harry bore this surname, and the word is also old slang for excellent.

parts.note: a buck is an old word for a fashionable young man, a dandy
hot can mean heated or angry

explanation.surface: Gunshot makes fops furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is coarse lead shot fired from a shotgun.

definitions.meaning: one of the writers of the three Synoptic Gospels, Matthew, Luke or the second evangelist
something aimed at, a goal or bull's-eye

explanation.definitionFit: The second Gospel writer is one of the Synoptists, and a target is something aimed at, as in 'hit the mark'.

definitions.meaning: stanzas of a poem or song

explanation.definitionFit: Stout sticks and stanzas of a poem both take this plural.

parts.note: the steady pulse of pop music, though it could read as a father's round or the beating Dad gives

explanation.surface: A father's patrol or his beating.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular pattern of beats in music, as in the pulse of a pop song.

clue.text: This bay's in Florida, thanks to new map

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: new says the word map is made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Florida bay found thanks to an up-to-date chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MAP into MPA, after TA, British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa Bay is a large inlet on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Up to that time was first left fallow

parts.note: up to that time means until then
to be first, in front, is to lead, so was first is led

explanation.surface: A field had been left uncultivated until then.
explanation.definitionFit: Untilled land has not been ploughed or cultivated, like ground left fallow.

clue.text: East European upset has to run away

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the nationality are knocked into a different order

parts.note: a Pole is a European, someone from Poland

explanation.surface: An Eastern European, distressed, has to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges POLE into LOPE, after E; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly, usually to marry.

definitions.meaning: to conceal a coin or card in the hand as a conjuror does
the Sunday before Easter takes this word as its name

explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror hides a card in the hand by this sleight, and the Sunday before Easter is named after the fronds strewn before Christ.

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the one nearest home; an inn is a pub
an ovation is applause, enthusiastic acclaim

explanation.surface: Something new attracting praise in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' here is the British word for a neighbourhood pub, so INN.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is a new idea, method or invention.

clue.text: Percolator for Swansea's head football coach

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a trainer coaches and prepares a football team

explanation.surface: Swansea City's top man is a coffee maker for the football coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Swansea is a Welsh city with a football club, which makes the surface look like sports news.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or filter that liquid percolates through.

clue.text: Swinburne's swallow, one of the family.

explanation.definitionFit: Swinburne addresses the swallow as a female sibling in Itylus, and a sibling is one of the family.
